title: The Future of High-Strength Aluminum: 7xxx Series Trends in Aerospace and Defense
summary: Market data on 7075 and 7050 aluminum demand through 2034. F-35 program requirements, UAV proliferation, carbon fiber cost comparison, and where 7xxx alloys win against composites.
body_text: $11.1B 7075-T6 aluminum market in 2024 Global Market Insights, 2025 $20.5B Projected 7075-T6 market by 2034 (6.5% CAGR) Global Market Insights, 2025 $28.8B Global UAV market in 2024 Fortune Business Insights Aluminum vs Carbon Fiber: Cost per Pound Structural material cost comparison ($/lb) 7075 aerospace plate (high end) 4 $/lb 7075 aerospace plate (low end) 1 $/lb CFRP prepreg (low end) 10 $/lb CFRP prepreg (high end) 65 $/lb Long-Cycle Programs Drive Baseline Demand The F-35 program exemplifies how a single long-cycle defense program generates sustained aluminum demand for decades. The F-35 airframe uses approximately 35% carbon fiber composites by structural weight, with aluminum and titanium making up the balance. 7050 aluminum is used in bulkheads and structural extrusions (Northrop Grumman F-35 Material Specifications; CompositesWorld). The program is projected to require over 50,000 metric tons of aerospace-grade aluminum through 2032 (24ChemicalResearch, 2024). With planned production rates of 150-plus aircraft per year through the 2030s, this is not a declining demand signal - it is a sustained procurement requirement that anchors the high-end aerospace aluminum market. The UAV Proliferation Effect The global UAV market reached approximately $28.8 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow by $37.53 billion between 2024 and 2029, with Fortune Business Insights projecting the market approaching $66 billion by 2032. The structural materials for small and medium tactical UAVs are overwhelmingly aluminum: 7075-T651 for primary load-bearing structure, 6061-T651 for secondary components. Unlike manned aircraft programs, UAV programs are iterative - designs change rapidly, production is often started before final design is locked, and material procurement follows a just-in-time pattern rather than long-term mill contracts. This creates sustained demand for stocking distributors who can respond to short-notice orders in the thickness ranges and origin requirements that defense programs specify. Carbon Fiber vs Aluminum: The Cost Reframe The narrative that composites are replacing aluminum in aerospace is directionally correct but incomplete. Aerospace-grade CFRP prepreg costs roughly an order of magnitude more per pound than structural aluminum plate, and specialty aerospace prepregs widen that gap further. At production volumes below approximately 5,000 units per program, aluminum is the economically dominant structural material. The crossover point shifts as composite manufacturing automation matures, but for the majority of defense programs measured in hundreds or low thousands of units, aluminum remains cheaper to procure, machine, inspect, and repair. CFRP fuselage panel production also consumes 30% more energy than equivalent aluminum extrusion, which is increasingly relevant for program sustainability requirements. Where Aluminum Cannot Compete: Hypersonics The hard physical limit for aluminum in structural applications is approximately 177 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit), above which the alloy's yield strength begins degrading rapidly. Hypersonic vehicles operating at Mach 5 and above generate aerothermal surface temperatures of 1,000 to 2,500 degrees Celsius - far beyond aluminum's operational range (AZoM; Nature Communications, 2024). Titanium alloys extend the range to approximately 600 degrees Celsius; above that, nickel superalloys (Inconel 625, 718) and ultra-high-temperature ceramics are required. Hypersonic structural applications represent a segment where aluminum is simply excluded, and where the growth in defense hypersonic programs is not a demand driver for standard 7xxx plate. New Alloy Development Arconic announced in early 2025 a new heat-treated 7xxx-series aluminum sheet offering 10% higher tensile strength and 20% better fatigue resistance for aircraft skins - improvements achieved through refined chemistry and thermal processing rather than adding alloy complexity. New generation 7xxx alloys are extending the performance envelope without requiring buyers to move to composites or titanium for structural applications. For buyers, the near-term implication is that standard 7075 and 7050 will remain the dominant procurement items while new alloy variants are qualified - aerospace qualification cycles typically run 3 to 7 years from initial characterization to approved supplier list inclusion.

title: Brownfield MDU Broadband: Unlocking Revenue with Existing Infrastructure
summary: Brownfield MDUs are a fast path to revenue. Reuse existing coax or fiber to deliver multi-gigabit broadband and speed deployment using legacy building infrastructure.
body_text: From Burden to Breakthrough Brownfield multi-dwelling unit ( MDUs) are often viewed as complex and costly to upgrade. In reality, many properties already have existing coax or fiber that can be leveraged, and residents in those buildings are demanding more bandwidth. With the right approach and technology, these legacy buildings can be transformed from perceived burdens into strategic assets that support new revenue and sustainable growth. The Brownfield Opportunity Rewiring a brownfield MDU triggers permits, unit access, and long construction windows. Crews move gear through halls, open ceilings, and drill walls, which creates dust, noise, and occasionally closes the elevator or corridor. Residents juggle appointments and brief cutovers, while property managers handle complaints, coordinate with contractors, and oversee security. The result can be slower deployments, higher labor and vendor costs, and underserved high-demand properties such as urban corridors with waitlists, student housing at term peaks, and work-from-home communities with heavy streaming and smart-home usage. Brownfield MDUs present a clear opportunity. Legacy coax and in-building fiber are installed assets that can be activated without full reconstruction. A reuse-first playbook treats existing plant as an on-ramp to multi-gigabit service, with fewer build steps, limited interior work, and more predictable cost control. This is the MDU Gold Mine: unlock value already in the building with the right solutions. Revenue, Not Renovation Brownfield MDUs are a scalable opportunity hiding in plain sight. Urban residents are streaming, gaming, working from home, and raising expectations for reliable bandwidth. Rather than pulling new fiber risers throughout the building and expanding outside plant or backbone segments, operators can activate multi-gigabit service by reusing in-building coax or fiber pathways and placing compact edge nodes at the property. By focusing on reusing existing infrastructure and rapid deployment, providers can achieve faster time to revenue, lower capital expenses, and improved customer quality of experience (QoE). 4 Ways to Turn Brownfield MDUs into Revenue Drivers Use What You Have Reusing existing coax or fiber eliminates the need for costly drilling or construction. For many brownfield buildings, a simple coax drop already exists to every unit. With DOCSIS 3.1, BoostD 3.1, or other compatible coax solutions, operators can activate multi-gigabit service with minimal disruption. Deploy at the Edge Compact, low-power nodes, such as SeaStar and Oyster , can be mounted on strands, poles, walls, or in cabinets. These bring capacity to the building's edge and enable service activation without waiting on permits or core construction. The result is faster installs and lower deployment risk. Minimize Disruption Prioritize low-impact deployment tailored to each building, keeping work outside where practical or in nonresidential spaces to limit tenant access, noise, and mess. This simplifies installation workflows, while accelerating rollout timelines and demonstrating a considerate approach to customer service. Accelerate ROI The less time and labor required to turn up service, the faster the revenue begins. Infrastructure reuse reduces labor costs, truck rolls, permitting cycles, and time spent inside buildings, allowing operators to realize ROI faster, even in challenging urban environments. Technology Snapshot: How It Works Without Rewiring Harmonic's SeaStar and Oyster MDU solutions deliver high-speed broadband by utilizing the existing building infrastructure. With support for both DOCSIS and PON architectures, they enable seamless integration into a wide range of environments, orchestrated by Harmonic's cOS™ broadband platform , which provides operators with a common management platform. For lower-density MDUs with fewer units, SeaStar lets operators centralize resources at the neighborhood level. A micro node at each MDU delivers service over existing coax, improving small site economics by supporting up to 16 MDUs within a 5 km radius. For large, higher-density MDUs, Oyster terminates the operator’s fiber at a central location, such as a utility room, and bridges to the in-building coax. Both SeaStar and Oyster preserve existing wiring and can deliver up to 8.5 Gbps downstream and 1.5 Gbps upstream, with an option to overlay 10G PON for fiber to the unit when needed. These deployment configurations enable operators to avoid rewiring while delivering high-speed performance and enhancing operational agility. Business Value Breakdown: From CAPEX Avoidance to OPEX Efficiency Treating brownfield MDUs as standard FTTH projects by bringing fiber to the building and bridging to coax inside offers clear benefits: Factor Traditional Fiber Overbuild Brownfield Infrastructure Reuse Deployment Time Long Short Installation Costs High Low Operational Complexity High Low Time to Revenue Slow Fast Operators reduce cost, complexity, and delay while accelerating revenue activation. Strategic Implications: From Niche to Norm Whether an operator starts from a legacy environment or is building a greenfield network, brownfield MDUs are no longer exceptions. Instead, they can be repeatable, cost-efficient deployment scenarios with substantial revenue growth opportunities. With SeaStar, Oyster, and the cOS™ platform, Harmonic enables multi-gigabit broadband for every MDU by activating existing in-building coax and fiber with remote devices. These solutions deliver a compact optionality for higher-density sites, serve multiple lower-density MDUs from a single neighborhood deployment, reduce costs, speed up installations, and require no rewiring, turning overlooked properties into an MDU gold mine. When building owners choose to invest in new fiber inside the property, Harmonic's solutions are ready. Operators can upgrade node units with a Fin OLT (Optical Line Terminal) to support XGS-PON (10 Gigabit-symmetrical Passive Optical Network) delivery, enabling fiber-to-the-unit functionality with zero node replacement. The Shortcut to Revenue is the Infrastructure You Already Own For years, brownfield MDUs have been considered risky, expensive, and unpredictable. Today, they are some of the fastest paths to new subscribers and new revenue—if approached the right way. By combining modern node technology, flexible deployment models, and a software-defined orchestration layer, Harmonic empowers operators to treat MDUs as a core part of their growth strategy. Brownfield is no longer a barrier. It is a business opportunity ready to be unlocked. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) What is a brownfield MDU, and why is it a revenue opportunity? A brownfield MDU is an existing multi-dwelling building with legacy wiring. By leveraging legacy in-building infrastructure, operators can deliver modern services with minimal construction and faster ROI. Can operators generate revenue from existing broadband infrastructure in MDUs? By reusing legacy coax or in-building fiber, operators can deliver multi-gigabit services faster and without rewiring, improving time to revenue, and reducing capital expenses How does Harmonic simplify brownfield deployments? Harmonic's SeaStar and Oyster MDU solutions enable broadband delivery over existing infrastructure. Combined with cOS™, these technologies provide centralized management, low-impact installs, and future upgrade paths.

title: RIVIA Strengthens Advisory Board with Appointment of Dr. Rich Christie to Accelerate Global Expansion in Clinical Trial Technology

body_text: Zurich, Switzerland – 19 Sep 2025 – RIVIA , the clinical trial intelligence company, today announced the appointment of Dr. Rich Christie, MD, PhD , as Strategic Advisor. This addition reflects RIVIA’s commitment to scaling its global presence and advancing integrated clinical trial technology solutions for biopharma sponsors worldwide. Dr. Christie brings over 25 years of experience at the intersection of clinical development, data science, and technology innovation. He has held senior R&D roles at Roche and Johnson & Johnson , and served as Chief Medical Officer at AiCure , where he helped pioneer the use of AI to transform clinical research. “Rich’s unique combination of medical, strategic, and technology expertise makes him an ideal advisor as RIVIA enters its next phase of growth,” said Erik Scalfaro, CEO and co-founder of RIVIA . “His insight into scalable, tech-enabled trial decision will help us broaden our impact and accelerate our mission to become the clinical trial intelligence backbone for biotechs globally.” Dr. Christie will work closely with Rivia’s leadership team to guide product strategy, market expansion, and partnerships with leading biotech sponsors. “I am excited to join Rivia at this pivotal moment,” said Dr. Christie . “RIVIA’s approach is reshaping how Biotechs make strategic decisions throughout clinical development. I look forward to helping the team expand their global footprint and bring these innovations to biotechs developing transformative therapies.” About RIVIA RIVIA is building the clinical trial intelligence platform that unifies data from across sources in real-time, from EDC, labs, imaging, EDC, and more, into trial workflows and strategic decisions. By combining zero-fault reliability with advanced analytics, Rivia empowers biotechs to accelerate development and deliver life-changing therapies.

title: Introducing Guardian
summary: Guardian is now available in Loops, launching alongside a set of improvements that refine your everyday experience across the product.
body_text: Release: Guardian Guardian is a lightweight, proactive filter set that lives in the email editor and Loop Builder actively alerting you and preventing mistakes. You will see it at the top of any campaign, loop or transactional email as a light checkmark when everything looks good but when an issue is detected it will make itself known with a colored notification dot. Helpful when you need it, out of your way when you don’t. Current checks include: Misplaced variables Unsaved changes (save state) Missing button links Missing fallbacks for dynamic content Have ideas for future guardrails? Just email [email protected] and tell us what to add next. Updates Supabase OAuth Support Head to the Supabase Settings inside Loops and use one-click OAuth to connect Supabase for SMTP setup. Start from any email in a Loop You can now start a new email in a Loop from any email in the current or another Loop. We also support starting from a Campaign or Transactional email (both published and draft states). Finally, we added a simple search filter to make it easier to find the exact email you’re looking for. UI redesign You may have noticed, the app got a bit of polish! This should make it a bit easier to parse large groups containing many emails. Some of the improvements we’ve made: Saving custom sorting by Updated, Sent and other top-level columns. Better drag-and-drop between groups as cards now shrink to a more manageable size and show a drop indicator. Block manual regrouping on system sorted emails. For example, if you sort ascending and attempt to drag, we’ll help you revert to your custom sort in one click. Better contrast on group headers. This improves accessibility and scanning on wide monitors. Most importantly, these changes introduced a new /groupId page. You can click the number next to a group, or the arrow on the far right, to open the group in a dedicated page. This makes bookmarking dedicated groups possible. For example, you can now create a dedicated bookmark for product updates without having to drill through the app every time. Additionally, the Loop Builder has had a light coat of paint to improve dark mode and smooth out some rough edges. Hiring update We’re excited to welcome Max to the team! Max was previously at Meta working on the Lexical framework, the text editor we use here at Loops. Max joining will help us extend and lay the foundation in the editor for what’s coming next. Everything else Better search You can now paste in a transactionalId , campaignId or loopId in the CMD+K (the search bar) in the app to filter and navigate to the given email. Mailing list support for incoming Webhooks Automatically add contacts piped in via incoming Webhooks (Stripe, Clerk, Supabase) to the mailing lists you’ve set up in Loops. Standardized API errors Every error now includes status and message to make it easier to process errors and integrate with your apps. Hit N to create a new email Press N on your keyboard anywhere in the app to start creating a new email! Paste in Markdown improvements We tweaked our formatter to account for soft breaks and a few other inconsistencies we noticed in markdown coming from third-party apps. Format text in buttons You can now bold text in buttons along with other text decorations.

title: Always On, Never Distracted: AI’s Role in Protecting Patients
body_text: Clinicians are being asked to manage increasingly complex patient profiles with limited time and resources. This challenge is especially pronounced in the care of patients with chronic conditions like heart failure, where the difference between proactive management and a reactive crisis can determine whether a patient recovers or is readmitted to the hospital. Dr. Ries Robinson, a leading voice in digital health innovation and a member of DocGo ’s Medical Advisory Board , believes artificial intelligence (AI) is a key part of the answer. The Human Limits of Reactive Monitoring Healthcare systems have developed strong capabilities for managing acute events. However, they often struggle with the sustained vigilance needed for chronic disease management. As Dr. Robinson explained: “Monitoring five parameters for one patient is something a clinician can do. But if you’re monitoring 20 people, each with five parameters, that becomes extremely difficult. And at scale, say 150 patients and beyond, it becomes impossible.” This information burden is compounded by the unique nature of each and every patient. What appears normal for one person may indicate a problem for someone else. In conditions such as heart failure, which can result from several distinct causes, each individual may exhibit a different physiological baseline. “Heart failure has many aetiologies,” Robinson noted. “Each can result in a different pattern of what is ‘normal’ for the patient. AI can help by identifying and tracking those individual baselines across multiple parameters. That’s not something the human brain is built to manage.” Hydration management offers another example: it requires deciphering the choreographed movement of water among intravascular, interstitial, and intracellular spaces, each reshaped minute?to?minute by salt intake, fluid loss, medications, and age. “Effective hydration management demands tools that fuse time?based kinetics, external disturbances, and three?compartment fluid flows into a single, actionable view,” Dr.?Robinson says. From Data Overload to AI Oversight Dr. Robinson sees three key opportunities for AI in patient monitoring: Managing Information Overload AI can process large volumes of data from hundreds of patients without fatigue. While human clinicians may miss early warning signs, AI can detect subtle changes and trends that often precede deterioration by continuously analyzing patterns in patient data and flagging gradual shifts that might be imperceptible to human observation. Establishing Individualized Baselines Rather than relying on generic population averages, AI can learn what is typical for each patient. This allows alerts to be based on personalized thresholds, supporting earlier and more accurate interventions. Supporting Medication Management Heart failure management often involves five separate classes of medication. AI can assist by tracking patient-specific medication response curves, identifying potential conflicts, and helping to ensure optimal combinations over time. Consistency, Focus, and Institutional Memory One often overlooked advantage of AI is its consistency. In hospitals, clinical focus shifts over time as institutional priorities change based on patient needs – potentially emphasizing fall prevention, hydration management or infection control. Staff naturally adapt their attention to the current initiative. Dr. Robinson shared a case from Presbyterian Hospital, where a targeted campaign to reduce patient falls initially succeeded. However, as leadership moved to new priorities, fall rates crept back up. “It was like whack-a-mole. People can only focus on one thing at a time. AI doesn’t have that limitation,” he said. Similarly, when experienced staff leave (whether due to retirement, rotation, or reassignment), it can lead to declines in patient outcomes. AI can help by preserving procedural knowledge, patient-specific knowledge, and institutional best practices. It provides continuity that human teams may struggle to maintain. The Indispensable Role of the Physician Although AI can deliver real-time insight and pattern recognition, it does not replace the physician’s role in decision-making. “The physician still plays a critical role, especially at the point of discharge where experience and intuition become critical,” Robinson added. “They’re the only ones with full visibility into comorbidities, the patient’s home support, and socio-economic context. AI can analyze data with dazzling speed, but does not have intuition—it cannot sense the undocumented interactions, emotions, and contextual nuances that make comfort and truly effective care possible.” These non-quantifiable factors still require clinical judgment. Shifting the Care Model Patient monitoring has traditionally been reactive: clinicians wait for a signal of deterioration and respond. AI enables a different approach; one that prioritizes safety through early detection, personalized baselines, and consistent oversight. This constant vigilance works best when paired with the irreplaceable clinical judgment that only physicians can provide. As Dr. Robinson put it: “AI’s unique advantage in remote patient monitoring is that it doesn’t get bored or distracted. So in the future you’ll be able to rest easy, knowing that the AI is always on the clock.”

title: Gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos: como realizar?
summary: Entenda o que é gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos, os principais tipos de ameaças e como proteger sua empresa com dados e tecnologia
body_text: A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos (SCRM) é um processo que identifica, avalia e controla ameaças que impactam o fluxo de abastecimento de um negócio. O objetivo é garantir a continuidade operacional e minimizar prejuízos que falhas logísticas, de fornecedores ou eventos inesperados possam causar. Esse tipo de gerenciamento ajuda a evitar perdas financeiras, atrasos nas entregas e interrupções que comprometem a produção e o atendimento ao cliente final. Quando aplicada com eficiência, a SCRM fortalece o relacionamento com empresas fornecedoras, melhora o planejamento e aumenta a resiliência da cadeia de suprimentos. Além disso, essa prática leva a decisões mais seguras, baseadas em informações concretas. Por esse motivo, a empresa ganha previsibilidade, mantém sua operação estável e preserva sua reputação no mercado. Para entender melhor e conhecer outras vantagens, continue a leitura deste artigo e descubra o que é, como funciona a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos e qual ferramenta usar para avaliar corretamente os fornecedores. Principais aprendizados: A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos identifica e controla ameaças com potencial de interromper o fluxo de abastecimento. A avaliação contínua de fornecedores evita falhas operacionais, financeiras e reputacionais que comprometem a supply chain. Planos de contingência garantem resposta rápida, minimizam impactos de situações adversas e aumentam a resiliência operacional. A diversificação de fornecedores e o uso de tecnologia são estratégias fundamentais para fortalecer a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos. Soluções, como o SRM da Linkana , automatizam etapas críticas e aumentam a eficiência na identificação e mitigação de riscos. O que é a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos (SCRM)? A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos é um processo que reúne diversas atividades para identificar ameaças com potencial de afetar negativamente o fluxo de abastecimento de uma empresa. Envolve análises, monitoramentos constantes e ações preventivas para garantir o funcionamento contínuo do negócio, mesmo diante de adversidades e imprevistos. A sigla que representa esse gerenciamento, SCRM, vem do termo em inglês Supply Chain Risk Management, e se trata de um procedimento essencial para o time responsável por compras e procurement reconhecer e se antecipar a possíveis problemas, como atrasos nas entregas, falhas nos contratos com os fornecedores, e mudanças regulatórias. Portanto, o objetivo é proteger a empresa contra riscos que comprometam sua estabilidade, cumprimento de prazos, margens de lucro , reputação e credibilidade. A SCRM também ajuda a reduzir custos com ajustes emergenciais, fortalecer as tomadas de decisão, aumentar a confiança operacional e a resiliência na cadeia de suprimentos. Aproveite e leia também: “ Gestão de riscos financeiros: realize com eficiência em 6 etapas! ” Como funciona a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos? A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos funciona como um processo estruturado para identificar, classificar, monitorar e tratar possíveis ameaças antes que impactem negativamente a operação da empresa. Cada etapa da cadeia de suprimentos, desde a escolha de fornecedores até a entrega dos produtos/serviços ao cliente final, deve passar por uma análise detalhada para o levantamento de pontos críticos e vulnerabilidades. Veja um exemplo de fluxo a seguir. Primeira etapa Inicia-se a SCRM pelo mapeamento completo da supply chain . Nessa fase, é necessário listar todos os agentes envolvidos nas operações, como fornecedores diretos e indiretos, prestadores de serviço, centros de distribuição e responsáveis pela parte logística. Esse primeiro diagnóstico revela em quais pontos estão as principais exposições a riscos operacionais, financeiros, ambientais e reputacionais. Segunda etapa Em seguida, a equipe responsável pela gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos deve realizar a análise das ameaças para classificá-las. A ideia é priorizar a tratativa daquelas que têm mais chances de acontecer, ou das que geram impacto mais significativo para as operações da empresa. A partir desse ponto, define-se um plano de contingência com medidas preventivas, protocolos de resposta rápida e indicadores de monitoramento contínuo, como índice de atraso de fornecedores, taxa de não conformidade em entregas, variações críticas de lead time ou mudanças no desempenho logístico. Terceira etapa Visto que os riscos em supply chain mudam com o passar do tempo, é fundamental acompanhar de forma ativa eventos com potencial de afetar o abastecimento, como instabilidades econômicas, mudanças regulatórias, escassez de matérias-primas, desastres naturais e conflitos geopolíticos . Outro ponto importante do funcionamento da SCRM é buscar a colaboração de fornecedores estratégicos . Compartilhar informações, estabelecer critérios claros de compliance na cadeia logística e adotar contratos com cláusulas de gestão de risco são medidas que fortalecem a relação entre as partes e reduzem a chance de surpresas. A melhor forma de colocá-las em prática é com a ajuda de um software de gerenciamento de relacionamento com fornecedores, um SRM . O SRM da Linkana, por exemplo, conecta a sua empresa e seus fornecedores de maneira simples e rápida. Também oferece diversos recursos de automação e o Linkana ESG Rating , ferramenta que avalia os riscos dos indicadores ambientais dos parceiros de abastecimento. Conheça! Quais são os principais riscos em supply chain? Estes são os principais riscos em supply chain: operacional; financeiro; dependência de fornecedor; regulatório e legal; geopolítico; climático e ambiental; de demanda; reputacional; tecnológico. Entenda cada um a seguir. Risco operacional Relaciona-se a falhas em processos internos ou de parceiros , como erros de produção, baixa qualidade nos insumos, atrasos logísticos e problemas de armazenagem. Eventos assim afetam diretamente prazos, custos e a capacidade de entrega ao consumidor final da empresa que contrata o abastecimento. Mitigar o risco operacional exige controle rigoroso de processos, alinhamento entre equipes, fornecedores e operadores logísticos, além de auditorias periódicas e análise de indicadores, como OTIF (On Time In Full) , índice de devoluções e nível de retrabalho. Risco financeiro Esse tipo de ameaça requer a análise da saúde econômica dos fornecedores, por meio da verificação de indicadores, como histórico de faturamento, nível de endividamento, liquidez, registros de protestos ou ações judiciais, certidões negativas e comportamento de pagamento no mercado. Também é recomendável acompanhar o score de crédito e, quando possível, solicitar balanços contábeis atualizados. Realizar esse levantamento é importante porque negócios com instabilidade financeira podem não cumprir contratos, gerar inadimplência ou até encerrar as atividades , o que compromete seriamente a continuidade do fornecimento. Risco de dependência de fornecedor Quando a empresa depende de um único fornecedor para itens críticos, qualquer falha nessa relação representa uma ameaça séria. A falta de alternativas aumenta a exposição a interrupções, reajustes de preços e perda de poder de negociação. Esse risco é ainda mais significativo quando o parceiro de abastecimento detém não apenas o fornecimento, mas também o conhecimento técnico, a customização do produto ou o acesso exclusivo a determinado insumo. Nessas situações, quem contrata perde autonomia e flexibilidade para reagir a atrasos, falhas contratuais ou mudanças repentinas nas condições comerciais. Risco regulatório e legal Mudanças em legislações trabalhistas, fiscais, ambientais ou comerciais impactam diretamente contratos e operações logísticas. O descumprimento de normas pode gerar multas, bloqueios ou paralisações. Para reduzir esse risco, o ideal é manter uma área jurídica ou de compliance atuante, com monitoramento constante da aplicação das leis em cada parte da cadeia de suprimentos. Também é essencial exigir dos fornecedores a apresentação de certidões atualizadas, licenças válidas, boas práticas ambientais e trabalhistas, além de incluir nos contratos cláusulas que prevejam penalidades claras em caso de irregularidades. Risco geopolítico Conflitos, embargos, instabilidades políticas e mudanças em políticas de importação/exportação interferem no acesso a mercados, rotas de transporte e disponibilidade de produtos vindos de determinadas regiões. Em situações assim, o ideal é**** diversificar a base de fornecedores **e buscar parceiros em países com estabilidade política e acordos comerciais mais previsíveis.** Também é interessante revisar periodicamente os contratos internacionais, prever cláusulas de salvaguarda (suspensão temporária) e manter estoques de segurança para itens críticos e importados. Risco climático e ambiental Eventos, como enchentes, secas, furacões e incêndios, afetam fluxos logísticos, acesso a centros de distribuição e operações agrícolas ou industriais. Além disso, exigem planos de resposta rápida. Uma das maneiras de mitigar esse risco é mapear geograficamente os fornecedores para identificar os mais expostos a desastres naturais e, se necessário, contratar parceiros mais próximos da empresa. Criar rotas alternativas, adotar estoques descentralizados e manter um banco de dados com fornecedores previamente qualificados são medidas que também ajudam a resolver esse tipo de ameaça. Risco de demanda Oscilações no consumo, sazonalidades mal planejadas e falhas de previsão causam excesso ou falta de estoque, o que gera perdas financeiras e reduz a eficiência da cadeia de suprimentos. Nesses casos, adotar ferramentas de previsão de demanda com base em dados históricos, inteligência de mercado e variáveis externas, como clima e tendências de consumo, aumenta a precisão no planejamento. Além disso, integrar as áreas de compras, vendas, marketing e logística favorece uma visão mais ampla e alinhada da demanda real, e reduz divergências sobre a real necessidade de compra. Risco de reputação Problemas provindos da dinâmica dos fornecedores, como trabalho escravo, corrupção ou práticas ambientais ilegais, prejudicam a imagem da empresa contratante. Em alguns setores, como os de alimentos e saúde, afeta diretamente a percepção do consumidor e o valor da marca. Para reduzir o risco reputacional, é essencial adotar políticas rigorosas de compliance na cadeia logística e de suprimentos, com critérios ESG bem definidos no processo de homologação e acompanhamento contínuo dos fornecedores. Ferramentas de due diligence automatizada e monitoramento reputacional, integradas a um SRM, como o da Linkana, ajudam a identificar e sinalizar comportamentos de risco e, assim, impedir o comprometimento da imagem de quem contratou o abastecimento. Risco tecnológico Falhas em sistemas, ataques cibernéticos, indisponibilidade de plataformas de gestão e uso de tecnologias obsoletas afetam a visibilidade da cadeia de suprimentos e impedem o monitoramento em tempo real. Por outro lado, plataformas modernas de Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), como a da Linkana, permitem visualizar de forma contínua os dados dos fornecedores, levantar e gerenciar riscos financeiros, reputacionais e operacionais. O uso desse tipo de tecnologia amplia o controle sobre a base de parceiros, garante mais agilidade na identificação de possíveis ameaças e aprimora a gestão de riscos da cadeia de suprimentos. Tenha em mente que mapear essas ameaças garante uma gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos mais estratégica, precisa e eficiente. No próximo tópico, explicaremos por quais motivos essa atividade é essencial para garantir a continuidade dos negócios. Antes, aprofunde-se nesse tema com as informações do artigo: “ Riscos na cadeia de suprimentos: quais são e como evitá-los? ” Por que a gestão de riscos é crítica para a continuidade dos negócios? A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos é crítica para a continuidade dos negócios, pois protege a empresa contra falhas que podem interromper o fluxo de materiais, comprometer a produção, elevar custos e afetar prazos de entrega aos clientes finais. Qualquer vulnerabilidade nos processos logísticos, sistemas operacionais ou modo de trabalho dos fornecedores tem potencial para se transformar em um gargalo que paralisa atividades essenciais e prejudica diretamente o desempenho da companhia. Além disso, riscos não tratados geram impactos financeiros sérios, seja por multas contratuais, perda de receita, queda no valor de mercado ou necessidade de gastos emergenciais para amenizar os danos. A reputação também sente o reflexo, pois um único episódio com fornecedores que realizam práticas ilegais consegue abalar a confiança de clientes, investidores e parceiros de negócio. Por outro lado, realizar uma boa gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos permite identificar previamente diferentes tipos de ameaças, criar planos de ação precisos e agir com rapidez quando as possibilidades se tornam reais. Quais as vantagens de realizar uma boa gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos? Quando aplicada com eficiência, a SCRM fortalece o relacionamento com fornecedores, melhora o planejamento empresarial e reduz a exposição a riscos que poderiam causar impactos graves. Além de potencializar a resposta a emergências, a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos permite decisões mais seguras, baseadas em informações concretas. Dessa forma, a empresa ganha previsibilidade, mantém sua operação estável, preserva a reputação no mercado, fortalece a governança e o negócio se torna mais estável, escalável e preparado para crescer, como um todo. Leia também: “ Governança corporativa: por que é importante e como implantar? ” Como fazer a avaliação de riscos de fornecedores? A avaliação de riscos de fornecedores consiste em identificar, analisar e monitorar potenciais ameaças que comprometam a entrega, a qualidade e a continuidade do fornecimento. Esse processo busca garantir o alinhamento dos parceiros de abastecimento aos padrões operacionais, financeiros, legais e éticos que a empresa contratante exige. Para realizar corretamente essa análise, é necessário: coletar informações detalhadas : solicitar aos fornecedores documentos fiscais, financeiros e certificações de qualidade, além de dados sobre práticas ambientais, trabalhistas e de compliance na cadeia logística; averiguar a saúde financeira : avaliar a situação econômica do fornecedor, por meio do resultado de diferentes indicadores, como liquidez, endividamento e histórico de inadimplência; verificar o fluxo operacional : como a capacidade produtiva, a qualidade dos insumos, o desempenho logístico, cumprimento de prazos, índices de retrabalho ou devoluções, por meio de visitas in loco ou auditorias; confirmar a compliance : por meio da conferência da conformidade com as legislações vigentes e a validade de licenças e autorizações; analisar a reputação : a partir da investigação do histórico de incidentes, reclamações de outros contratantes, práticas éticas e sustentabilidade de fontes confiáveis, como listas de sanções nacionais e internacionais, portais de notícias e levantamento de processos judiciais. É importante destacar que a avaliação de riscos de fornecedores deve ser contínua, e não apenas no momento que antecede a contratação. Inclusive, integrá-la a sistemas de gestão facilita o acompanhamento das mudanças do perfil dos fornecedores e ajuda a reagir mais rapidamente a qualquer sinal de alerta. A adoção de plataformas tecnológicas, como as soluções SRM da Linkana, agiliza esse processo, automatiza a coleta de dados e fornece dashboards com indicadores em tempo real, o que otimiza as tomadas de decisão. Entenda mais no artigo: “ Análise de risco de fornecedores: como fazer e 4 erros a evitar! ” 7 estratégias de mitigação e resposta aos riscos na cadeia A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos exige ações coordenadas e preventivas para reduzir vulnerabilidades, aumentar a resiliência operacional e proteger o fluxo de abastecimento frente a imprevistos. Adotar boas estratégias ajuda a identificar ameaças e respondê-las com eficiência. Veja a seguir as práticas mais indicadas. 1. Diversificar a base de fornecedores Depender de um único parceiro de abastecimento deixa a rede de supply chain fraca. Já com uma base diversificada, com alternativas qualificadas, reduz-se o risco de ruptura e aumenta-se o poder de negociação. 2. Monitorar continuamente os parceiros de abastecimento Acompanhar o desempenho, as condições financeiras, a conformidade legal e o histórico reputacional dos fornecedores permite identificar mudanças de perfil e agir antes que pequenos sinais se transformem em falhas operacionais graves. 3. Mapear e classificar os riscos Identificar, documentar e categorizar os riscos por grau de impacto e probabilidade facilita priorizar ações. Esse mapeamento é essencial para estruturar planos de resposta e distribuir recursos financeiros e humanos de forma mais inteligente. 4. Criar planos de contingência e resposta a incidentes Simular cenários ajuda a criar planos de ação específicos para cada tipo de risco e garante agilidade e organização na aplicação desse planejamento em situações reais. Considere, por exemplo, alternativas de fornecimento, fluxos de comunicação e protocolos de recuperação rápida. 5. Fechar parcerias estratégicas Manter relações próximas, baseadas em confiança e transparência, favorece o alinhamento de expectativas e a cooperação em momentos difíceis. Fornecedores envolvidos nas decisões da cadeia de suprimentos tendem a colaborar de forma mais ativa na implementação de soluções. 6. Realizar auditorias e avaliações periódicas Realizar auditorias técnicas, operacionais e de compliance ajuda a manter o controle de qualidade e garantir que os fornecedores sigam os padrões que a empresa exige. Essa prática também reforça a cultura de responsabilidade na rede de abastecimento. 7. Automatizar processos com ajuda da tecnologia Plataformas de SRM e soluções baseadas em dados, como a da Linkana, permitem visualizar riscos em tempo real, automatizar alertas e padronizar análises. Essa dinâmica reduz falhas humanas e amplia a capacidade de resposta diante de variações na cadeia. Qual o papel da tecnologia e dos dados na gestão de riscos de fornecedores? A gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos depende, prioritariamente, de dados. Contudo, é essencial extraí-los de fontes confiáveis, auditáveis e atualizadas, mas realizar esse levantamento de forma manual demanda tempo, aumenta as chances de erros e de deixar informações importantes passarem despercebidas. Além disso, a automação ajuda a organizar, cruzar e analisar os dados com mais agilidade, o que torna as decisões mais rápidas, estratégicas e menos sujeitas a falhas humanas. Ferramentas tecnológicas voltadas para a gestão de fornecedores, como plataformas SRM, permitem centralizar toda a documentação, acompanhar indicadores de risco em tempo real e obter alertas com base em critérios que a empresa contratante define. Essa dinâmica reduz o retrabalho, evita perdas de prazos e facilita o cumprimento de requisitos regulatórios. Outro ponto importante é que usar a tecnologia na gestão de riscos da cadeia de suprimentos viabiliza o monitoramento contínuo da base de parceiros de abastecimento, o que permite reações imediatas diante de mudanças no perfil financeiro, jurídico, operacional ou reputacional. O uso de Inteligência Artificial e algoritmos avançados, como os de machine learning e análise preditiva, também contribui para prever comportamentos de risco com base em históricos e padrões. Além da eficiência operacional, o uso de dados e automação fortalece a transparência nos processos, melhora o relacionamento com os fornecedores e facilita auditorias internas e externas. O resultado é uma cadeia de suprimentos mais segura, rastreável e preparada para responder a cenários de crise com muito mais controle e precisão. Como a Linkana apoia a SCRM com automação e inteligência? A Linkana apoia a SCRM com automação e inteligência ao entregar um sistema completo, com funcionalidades que aceleram de ponta a ponta as atividades relacionadas ao gerenciamento de parceiros de abastecimento. A plataforma padroniza e agilita o cadastro e homologação de fornecedores, elimina tarefas manuais e garante a coleta automática de documentos, certificados e informações fiscais, ambientais e trabalhistas. O monitoramento de vencimentos e pendências ocorre em tempo real, por meio de alertas configuráveis que ajudam a manter a conformidade sempre em dia. O sistema da Linkana também é integrável a diversos softwares, como ERP e de compras, o que otimiza o aproveitamento de dados e as consultas. Conte ainda com outras funcionalidades, como o Linkana ESG Rating, dashboards inteligentes e workflows automatizados, e realize uma gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos muito mais prática, dinâmica e precisa. Quer conferir todas as nossas soluções, na prática? Então, preencha o formulário abaixo e solicite uma demonstração **** do SRM da Linkana. FAQ O que é SCRM e qual é a sua importância para as empresas? SCRM, ou gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos, é o processo de identificar, avaliar e mitigar ameaças ao abastecimento. Sua importância está em proteger a operação contra falhas, garantir continuidade e reduzir diversos prejuízos, como financeiros, legais e reputacionais. Quais são os principais riscos na cadeia de suprimentos? Os principais riscos são: operacional, financeiro, dependência de fornecedor, regulatório e legal, geopolítico, climático e ambiental, de demanda, reputacional e tecnológico. Essas ameaças podem impactar prazos, custos e a imagem da empresa. Por esse motivo, exigem monitoramento e estratégias específicas de mitigação. Como mapear riscos na base de fornecedores? Mapear riscos envolve coletar dados sobre histórico, desempenho, situação financeira, conformidade legal e reputação dos fornecedores. A análise contínua desses indicadores, juntamente com auditorias e uso de ferramentas digitais, permite identificar vulnerabilidades e priorizar ações preventivas e corretivas. Quais tecnologias ajudam na gestão de riscos em supply chain? Plataformas SRM, automação, inteligência artificial, machine learning, análise preditiva e integração com ERPs, são exemplos de tecnologias que facilitam a gestão de riscos por oferecer monitoramento em tempo real, avaliação de fornecedores e respostas rápidas, o que aumenta a visibilidade e a eficiência desse gerenciamento. Como a Linkana apoia a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos? A Linkana apoia a gestão de riscos na cadeia de suprimentos ao entregar uma plataforma automatizada para cadastro, monitoramento e avaliação contínua de fornecedores. O sistema é integrável a outros softwares e oferece diferentes recursos, como o Linkana ESG Rating, o que garante a conformidade, transparência e agilidade no controle de ameaças à rede de abastecimento.

body_text: ‹ Back Allarity Therapeutics CEO to Present at Biomarkers & Precision Medicine 2025 17/09/2025 TARPON SPRINGS, Fla., September 17, 2025 – Allarity Therapeutics, Inc. (“Allarity” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: ALLR), a Phase 2 clinical-stage pharmaceutical company dedicated to developing stenoparib—a differentiated, dual PARP and WNT pathway inhibitor—today announced that its CEO, Thomas Jensen, has been invited to present at the upcoming Biomarkers & Precision Medicine 2025 conference in London, organized by Oxford Global. In addition to his presentation, Mr. Jensen will be interviewed by Oxford Global’s editorial team to provide further insights into Allarity’s research and its innovative DRP® companion diagnostic platform. The interview will be featured on Oxford Global’s online content portal. Presentation Details: Event: Biomarkers & Precision Medicine 2025 Presentation Title: A Gene Expression Based Biomarker For Predicting Response To Treatment With Stenoparib Date: Wednesday, October 1, 2025 Time: 4:00 PM Mr. Jensen will be available for individual meetings during the conference to explore business development prospects. Attendees are encouraged to book one-on-one sessions in advance. About Stenoparib Stenoparib is an orally available, small-molecule dual-targeted inhibitor of PARP1/2 and tankyrase 1/2. At present, tankyrases are attracting significant attention as emerging therapeutic targets for cancer, principally due to their role in regulating the WNT signaling pathway. Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling has been implicated in the development and progression of numerous cancers. By inhibiting PARP and blocking WNT pathway activation, stenoparib’s unique therapeutic action shows potential as a promising therapeutic for many cancer types, including ovarian cancer. Allarity has secured exclusive global rights for the development and commercialization of stenoparib, which was originally developed by Eisai Co. Ltd. and was formerly known under the names E7449 and 2X-121. About the Drug Response Predictor – DRP ® Companion Diagnostic Allarity uses its drug-specific DRP® to select those patients who, by the gene expression signature of their cancer, may have a high likelihood of benefiting from a specific drug. By screening patients before treatment, and only treating those patients with a sufficiently high, drug-specific DRP score, the therapeutic benefit rate may be enhanced. The DRP method builds on the comparison of sensitive vs. resistant human cancer cell lines, including transcriptomic information from cell lines, combined with clinical tumor biology filters and prior clinical trial outcomes. DRP is based on messenger RNA expression profiles from patient biopsies. The DRP® platform has shown an ability to provide a statistically significant prediction of the clinical outcome from drug treatment in cancer patients across dozens of clinical studies (both retrospective and prospective). The DRP platform, which may be useful in all cancer types and is patented for dozens of anti-cancer drugs, has been extensively published in the peer-reviewed literature. About Allarity Therapeutics Allarity Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALLR) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to developing personalized cancer treatments. The Company is focused on development of stenoparib, a novel PARP/tankyrase inhibitor for advanced ovarian cancer patients, using its DRP® technology to develop a companion diagnostic that can be used to select those patients expected to derive the greatest clinical benefit from stenoparib. Allarity is headquartered in the U.S., with a research facility in Denmark, and is committed to addressing significant unmet medical needs in cancer treatment. For more information, visit www.allarity.com . title: VirnetX Facilities Receive Critical Department of Defense Security Certification
summary: DD Form 2345 Certification Reinforces Strategic Shift Toward Department of Defense and Intelligence Community Focus ZEPHYR COVE, Nev. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 4, 2025-- VirnetX Holding Corporation (NYSE: VHC), a global leader in secure communications and zero-trust cybersecurity solutions, today
body_text: View printer-friendly version << Back Press Release September 4, 2025 at 9:25 AM EDT VirnetX Facilities Receive Critical Department of Defense Security Certification DD Form 2345 Certification Reinforces Strategic Shift Toward Department of Defense and Intelligence Community Focus ZEPHYR COVE, Nev.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 4, 2025-- VirnetX Holding Corporation (NYSE: VHC), a global leader in secure communications and zero-trust cybersecurity solutions, today announced that it has received DD Form 2345 certifications for its two facilities in Zephyr Cove, Nevada, and Farmington, Utah. This achievement represents a significant milestone in the company’s evolution from a primarily commercial provider toward its goal of becoming a dedicated partner for the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) and Intelligence Community (IC). The DD Form 2345, formally known as the Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement, is a certification administered by the DoD’s Joint Certification Program. It enables certified organizations to access unclassified technical data with military or space applications that are subject to export controls under the Export Administration Regulations or International Traffic in Arms Regulations. This certification is essential for contractors, including technology companies like VirnetX, to handle and share sensitive technical information without compromising national security. Acquiring the DD Form 2345 is critically important for companies seeking to engage with the DoD and IC, as it unlocks opportunities to participate in classified projects, collaborate on defense initiatives, and bid on government contracts that require access to controlled data. For VirnetX, this certification corroborates the company’s robust security protocols and positions it to deliver its patented zero-trust platforms, designed for resilient, secure communications across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments, to mission-critical applications in land, sea, air, space, and cyber domains. It underscores VirnetX’s strategic pivot, allowing the company to expand in the defense sector with its Digital Engineering services that advance Model-Based Systems Engineering and align with the DoD’s Digital Engineering strategy. VirnetX embeds secure communications along with its Dynamic Trust Evaluation for the purpose of ensuring resilient networks. The Company’s product portfolio is designed to secure command and control, battle management, and multi-domain sensor orchestration, while its Cyber Threat Intelligence services deliver insights, empowering defense leaders to anticipate and counter emerging threats. “We are excited to announce this certification which reinforces our commitment to national security and innovation,” said Kendall Larsen, VirnetX CEO and President. “As we transition our focus toward serving the DoD and IC, the DD Form 2345 empowers us to provide cutting-edge, zero-trust solutions that protect sensitive communications and data in an increasingly complex threat landscape. This is a game-changer for VirnetX and our partners as it strengthens our shift to broader industry trends toward enhanced government collaboration, enabling the company to contribute to vital programs that safeguard U.S. interests.” About VirnetX VirnetX Holding Corporation is an Internet security software and technology company specializing in patented Zero Trust Network Access (“ZTNA”) for secure network communications. The Company’s solutions, including its Secure Domain Name Registry and its flagship platform, VirnetX One™, and products like War Room™ and VirnetX Matrix™, are designed to be device and location independent and enable secure real-time communication environments for U.S. defense, intelligence, and government agencies, as well as enterprise applications and critical infrastructure. The Company also offers Digital Engineering services that align with defense strategies, including its comprehensive Cyber Threat Assessment services and Model-Based System Engineering processes. For more information, please visit www.virnetx.com . title: Hesai Recognized on Fortune's 2025 Change the World List for Redefining Road Safety
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Hesai Technology (NASDAQ:HSAI and HKEX:2525), the global leader in lidar solutions, has been named by Fortune, a global multiplatform media...
body_text: PALO ALTO, Calif. , Sept. 25, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Hesai Technology (NASDAQ: HSAI and HKEX:2525), the global leader in lidar solutions, has been named by Fortune, a global multiplatform media company, to its prestigious 2025 Change the World list. Each year, Fortune's Change the World list highlights 50 of the world's most innovative companies that create meaningful social or environmental impact through their core business strategies. Hesai is the only lidar company to be featured this year, joining industry leaders such as Alibaba, Deloitte, Mastercard, and Schneider Electric. Fortune editors recognized Hesai's significant contributions to the Public Health and Safety sector by bringing lidar to the mass market and transforming vehicle safety worldwide. title: We analyzed 66,821 GitHub Actions runs: 9 hidden gems you're missing
summary: We analyzed 66,821 GitHub Actions workflow runs to uncover valuable third-party actions that teams are using to speed up CI pipelines and improve developer productivity. The data reveals hidden gems in the Actions marketplace that could transform your workflows.
body_text: Do you stick to official GitHub Actions in your workflows? Makes sense. Why risk your CI pipeline on some random third-party action? Turns out, the biggest CI wins could be hiding in the actions marketplace, where other developers have solved the exact problems you're facing. We analyzed 66,821 workflow runs across all organizations using Depot's runners to uncover the third-party GitHub Actions ecosystem. The results revealed some hidden gems that could transform your workflows. Scope of third-party adoption 189 third-party actions with multi-organization adoption (we filtered out single-organization actions to focus on broadly useful tools) 63 authors/organizations As you’d expect, the actions run the gamut from specialized tools for specific languages to general productivity enhancers. 9 third-party actions that are worth your time Depot customers are concerned about CI speed and naturally have adopted actions to speed up performance. Here are 9 actions with relatively low adoption that deliver significant value. 1. Build step optimization dorny/paths-filter - Used by 11% of organizations I think this is super cool. This action detects which files changed in a PR and sets outputs you can use to conditionally run jobs. It’s great when you want to control running individual jobs or steps only when certain file changes happen. - uses : dorny/paths-filter@v3 id : changes with : filters : | backend: - 'src/api/**' frontend: - 'src/web/**' - name : Run backend tests if : steps.changes.outputs.backend == 'true' run : pnpm run test:api 2. Fast Python package management astral-sh/setup-uv - Used by 7% of organizations Installing Python dependencies can take a really long time. Astral’s uv comes to the rescue. For my most recent Python project, I’ve switched over to uv and am getting about 6x faster installs. It’s great. By default the astral-sh/setup-uv action caches and that makes things even better. - uses : astral-sh/setup-uv@v6 - name : Install dependencies run : uv pip install -r requirements.txt 3. Compilation caching mozilla-actions/sccache-action - Used by 6% of organizations We're always trying to speed up compiles. This action speeds up compilation for Rust, C++, and other compiled languages by caching compilation results across CI runs. Depot runners are already set up to use sccache to speed up builds . For rocker, my Rust rewrite of docker, using sccache cut the build and test time by half. - uses : mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.9 - name : Build project run : RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo build --release 4. System package caching awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action - Used by 2% of organizations In CI, installing packages from apt can take a long time. This action can cache packages eliminating repeated package downloads and installations. There are caveats if your package has pre- or post-scripts. Well worth a try. - uses : awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action@v1 with : packages : libssl-dev 5. Robust CI pipelines nick-fields/retry - Used by 4% of organizations As much as we engineers don’t want it to be true, it’s not uncommon for tests to be flaky. nick-fields/retry can automatically retry failed steps with configurable backoff. I’m not exactly sure how to categorize this one; feels like it removes some of the need to restart CI runs, so, performance? In any case, it might be controversial, but it’s definitely pragmatic. - uses : nick-fields/retry@v3 with : timeout_minutes : 10 max_attempts : 3 command : pnpm run integration-tests 6. Better PR feedback marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment - Used by 4% of organizations Updates a single comment on PRs. This is nice as it can help reviewers get context from a PR instead of digging through CI logs. This example shows how to put the contents of a file as a comment in the PR. - uses : marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2 with : path : coverage-results.md 7. Beautiful test result reports dorny/test-reporter - Used by 3% of organizations Another nice action by dorny . With this test failures are immediately visible in PR checks with detailed context. For me, it is pretty painful to search through go test logs for the word fail . Too many tests or logs have that as their name! Here is a way to get a nice simplified view. I should note that this supports more than go tests! - name : Run tests run : go test -json ./... > testresults.json - name : Test Report uses : dorny/test-reporter@v2 with : name : Go Tests path : testresults.json reporter : golang-json 8. Universal binary installer taiki-e/install-action - Used by 3% of organizations This simplifies and speeds up getting the right tools into the CI environment. It installs precompiled binaries from GitHub releases with automatic caching and platform detection. The GitHub repo includes a list of all the tools it supports ready to go. Really nice and simple. - uses : taiki-e/install-action@v2 with : tool : cargo-nextest,just,cargo-hack 9. Enforce PR standards amannn/action-semantic-pull-request - Used by 3% of organizations I mean, I like and use conventional commits, but I figure your commit message is your own. If you want to enforce semantic PR titles for automated changelogs and better commit history, you can use this. - uses : amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@v5 with : types : | fix feat docs ci chore Honorable mentions The downside of having a really interesting dataset is that you have to pick only a few. I figured I’d share a few more metrics as bellwethers for our industry. AI and automation : anthropics/claude-code-action - AI-powered code review (4% adoption) Testing and quality : chromaui/action - Visual regression testing (3% adoption) cypress-io/github-action - E2E testing with zero config (3% adoption) codecov/codecov-action - Coverage reporting (7% adoption) Infrastructure : pulumi/actions - Infrastructure as code deployments (3% adoption) hashicorp/setup-terraform - Terraform workflows (4% adoption) Security and secrets : dopplerhq/cli-action - Centralized secrets management (3% adoption) 1password/load-secrets-action - 1Password integration (<1% adoption) Language-specific : pnpm/action-setup - Fast Node.js package management (17% adoption) ruby/setup-ruby - Ruby environment setup (5% adoption) dtolnay/rust-toolchain - Rust toolchain management (6% adoption) oven-sh/setup-bun - Bun JavaScript runtime (6% adoption) The bottom line The GitHub Actions third-party ecosystem has matured into a sophisticated toolkit where specialized solutions often outperform general-purpose alternatives. Maybe it's time to see what you're missing? Related posts Faster GitHub Actions with Depot Comparing GitHub Actions and Depot runners for 2x faster builds Faster Claude Code agents in GitHub Actions Chris Goller Principal Software Engineer at Depot

title: Tyson Foods Announces Executive Leadership Appointment
summary: Tyson Foods, Inc. announced the appointment of Devin Cole as Chief Operating Officer (COO). As COO, Devin will oversee the company’s business segments, including Poultry, Beef, Pork, Prepared Foods and International.
body_text: SPRINGDALE, Ark. – September 2, 2025 – Tyson Foods, Inc. (NYSE: TSN) today announced the appointment of Devin Cole as Chief Operating Officer (COO). As COO, Devin will oversee the company’s business segments, including Poultry, Beef, Pork, Prepared Foods and International. Devin will continue to report to Donnie King, Tyson Foods President and Chief Executive Officer. Devin has a proven track record with more than 30 years of experience in the industry, and his appointment reflects Tyson Foods’ commitment to robust succession planning and operational excellence. Most recently, Devin served as Group President of Poultry and International, where he delivered the company's third consecutive quarter of volume growth in Poultry and improved profitability to our International business by driving efficiencies and cost controls. “We have strong momentum as we head into our new fiscal year, and we remain committed to executing our long-term strategy and operating the company guided by our culture and Core Values. I am confident that under Devin’s leadership our business will continue to thrive,” noted Donnie King, CEO. Brady Stewart will be departing the company, effective immediately. The company determined certain actions taken by Brady violated the Tyson Foods Code of Conduct. With Brady's departure, the Supply Chain, Food Safety, Health and Safety, Environmental and Transportation functions will report directly to Donnie. The company will share further leadership and organizational updates prior to September 28, 2025 – the start of its 2026 fiscal year – consistent with its established succession planning and governance processes. ### About Tyson Foods, Inc. Tyson Foods, Inc. (NYSE: TSN) is a world-class food company and recognized leader in protein. Founded in 1935 by John W. Tyson, it has grown under four generations of family leadership. The Company is unified by this purpose: Tyson Foods. We Feed the World Like Family™ and has a broad portfolio of iconic products and brands including Tyson®, Jimmy Dean®, Hillshire Farm®, Ball Park®, Wright®, State Fair®, Aidells® and ibp®. Tyson Foods is dedicated to bringing high-quality food to every table in the world, safely and affordably, now and for future generations. Headquartered in Springdale, Arkansas, the company had approximately 138,000 team members on September 28, 2024. Visit www.tysonfoods.com .

title: Prompting Part 12: Harnessing the Power of Prompt Orchestration
summary: Discover how orchestrating a sequence of specialized prompts can create comprehensive, custom solutions for different roles within an organization. Understanding how to combine these prompts effectively can elevate your analytical capabilities.
body_text: As we wrap up our deep dive into Moody’s Research Assistant, it’s time to bring together all the insights we’ve explored over the past 12 weeks. We’ve examined how tailored prompts can transform workflows for various personas, enhancing productivity and precision in financial analysis. In this final post, we’ll showcase how orchestrating a sequence of specialized prompts can create comprehensive, custom solutions for different roles within an organization. Whether you’re a credit analyst, investment banker, or portfolio manager, understanding how to combine these prompts effectively can significantly elevate your analytical capabilities. The Art of Prompt Orchestration Organizations, teams, and individual roles often require unique approaches to financial assessments. By strategically combining custom prompts, users can build workflows that address specific needs, ensuring that each step of the analysis is thorough and tailored. Let’s explore how this orchestration works for three key personas: credit analyst, investment banker, and portfolio manager. Credit Analyst - Issuer Report Workflow Objective: Conduct a deep-dive fundamental credit analysis on a specific company to prepare an internal report. This workflow transitions from a broad overview to detailed scrutiny of peers and financial metrics. Prompts and Their Impact: Company Overview Prompt: Write a company overview for [ENTITY] including its business model, revenue streams by segment, and management team. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: This prompt synthesizes qualitative data from various reports into a cohesive narrative, providing a solid foundation of the company's operations and leadership. Rating History Prompt: Show [ENTITY]'s rating history for the last 5 years in a table. Include the rating action date, type, and a one-sentence summary for each change. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: By quickly pulling rating data and summarizing the qualitative reasoning behind each rating change, this prompt offers a clear view of the company’s credit trajectory over time. Credit Analysis (Up/Down Factors, Strengths and Weaknesses) Prompt: Summarize the key credit strengths and weaknesses for [ENTITY], including factors that could lead to an upgrade or downgrade. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: This prompt delves into Moody’s credit opinions, extracting core arguments to highlight the main factors influencing the company's credit status. It moves the analysis beyond raw data to provide actionable insights. Financials Advanced Query Prompt: List the 2023 financial performance for [ENTITY]. Calculate the year-over-year percentage change. Value: Automating the gathering and calculation of financial data streamlines the process, allowing you to focus on interpreting the numbers rather than compiling them. Peer Comparison Advanced Query Prompt: Compare [ENTITY]'s 2023 DEBT/EBITDA, EBITA MARGIN %, FCF/DEBT to the average of their peers. Value: This performs calculations across datasets, benchmarking the target company against its peers. It provides a comparative perspective on the company’s financial health. Recent Updates (Earnings) Prompt: Summarize the key themes from [ENTITY]'s most recent earnings call, focusing on forward guidance and management's response to analyst questions on EV profitability. Sources: Moody’s Data and Earnings Calls Value: By summarizing unstructured information from earnings call transcripts, this prompt offers the most up-to-date, forward-looking insights, enhancing the relevance of the credit assessment. Investment Banker - Pitch Deck Creation Workflow Objective: Screen for potential acquisition targets and generate a high-level summary for an initial pitch deck. This workflow emphasizes speed and efficiency, beginning with broad screening before narrowing down to specific targets. Prompts and Their Impact: Screen for Acquisition Targets Advanced Query Prompt: List of European airline companies with a rating of Ba1 or lower, revenue over $2 billion and positive free cash flow in 2024. Include 2024 Revenue, Net Debt/EBITDA, and EBITA Margin. Value: This builds a potential target list by layering financial thresholds, generating a clean table that’s ready for presentations and discussions. Business Profile Prompt: Write a one-paragraph business profile for [ENTITY]. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: By generating a qualitative summary, this prompt prepares essential content for the "Target Overview" slide in the pitch deck, ensuring a concise and informative introduction to each potential target. SWOT Analysis Prompt: Perform a SWOT analysis for [ENTITY] and its top 2 peers in a table format. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: This prompt synthesizes Moody’s research into a structured SWOT framework, providing a quick and clear view of the competitive landscape and strategic positioning of each company. Latest News Prompt: Summarize the latest news for [ENTITY] from the last 3 months with a positive or neutral sentiment. Sources: Moody’s Data & News Value: Acting as a final check, this prompt ensures there are no recent negative headlines that could impact the attractiveness of the acquisition target, safeguarding the pitch’s integrity. Portfolio Manager - Risk Monitoring Workflow Objective: Monitor macro sector risks and assess the health of a specific holding within the portfolio against key risk indicators. This workflow focuses on understanding overarching risks and pinpointing specific vulnerabilities within portfolio holdings. Prompts and Their Impact: Market Risk Analysis Prompt: What are the top 5 risks facing the UK banking sector currently Sources: Moody’s Data Value: Starting at the macro level, this prompt addresses broad, thematic questions to grasp the current operating environment, providing context for the portfolio’s risk assessment. Benchmark Analysis Advanced Query Prompt: Calculate the 2024 median key indicators for the UK banking sector. In a column, include [ENTITY]'s reported and adjusted 2024 key indicators Value: Establishing a quantitative baseline, this prompt benchmarks the health of the sector and identifies whether specific holdings are underperforming or outperforming relative to their peers. Rating Change Triggers Prompt: In a table, detail HSBC's upgrade and downgrade thresholds. Include most recent adjusted performance in relation to these thresholds. Sources: Moody’s Data Value: Visualizing key risk metrics against critical thresholds provides an instant view of the company's position, highlighting its proximity to potential rating changes. Credit Event Analysis Advanced Query Prompt: List of any UK banking companies that have had a rating downgrade or outlook change to negative in the past 6 months. Value: This portfolio monitoring query scans for recent negative credit events, signaling potential contagion risks that could affect the broader sector or specific holdings. Outlook Prompt: What is the outlook for the European banking sector and why Data: Moody’s Data Value: Ensuring that the latest comprehensive research from Moody’s analysts is reviewed, this prompt confirms the overall findings and projections, providing a forward-looking perspective on sector health. Bringing It All Together Prompt orchestration isn’t just a technical tool — it’s a smarter, faster way to work with greater confidence. Moody's Research Assistant integrates seamlessly into your workflows, optimizing processes, automating repetitive tasks, and empowering you to tackle complex challenges. Whether it’s credit analysis, pitch deck creation, or portfolio risk monitoring, it adapts to your needs so you can focus on what matters most. Throughout our Summer Prompting Series, we’ve shown how targeted prompts can simplify complex tasks and deliver actionable insights in no time. As the financial landscape evolves, mastering prompt orchestration will help you make better-informed decisions and uncover new opportunities. While this series concludes, your journey with Moody’s Research Assistant is just beginning — and we’re here to help you every step of the way. About the author: Caroline Hedgcock is an Assistant Director of Customer Success at Moody’s, where she specializes in helping clients optimize their use of Moody’s Research Assistant. A leader in AI prompting strategies, Caroline works closely with financial institutions to streamline workflows, accelerate analysis, and unlock deeper insights leveraging Moody’s GenAI-powered Research Assistant. With extensive expertise in applying advanced prompting techniques, Caroline ensures that clients harness the full capabilities of the Research Assistant to enhance decision-making and operational efficiency. Her approach bridges technical innovation with practical application, helping organizations unlock the benefits of embedding GenAI into their daily workflows.
